sub_unit_name: Introduction, Calorific value of fuel HCV, LCV- Dulongs formula

content.title: Fuel and Calorific Value
content.description: A fuel is a substance that produces heat energy when burned in the presence of oxygen. The amount of heat released by the complete combustion of unit quantity of fuel is called its calorific value.

content.content: Calorific value is one of the most important properties of a fuel. It indicates the energy content of the fuel and helps in selecting suitable fuels for domestic, industrial, and power generation applications.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Fuels with higher calorific value produce more heat and are generally more efficient and economical.
Calorific Value (CV) is the quantity of heat produced by the complete combustion of unit mass (or unit volume) of a fuel. It is usually expressed in kJ/kg for solid and liquid fuels.

rows: Includes the latent heat of condensation of water vapour formed during combustion.
Does not include the latent heat of water vapour; hence it is always lower than HCV.

content.content: Dulong's formula is an empirical equation used to calculate the Higher Calorific Value (HCV) of a fuel from its elemental composition.

content.title: Dulong's Formula
content.code:
HCV (kcal/kg) = (1/100) × [8080C + 34500(H - O/8) + 2240S]

Where:
C = % Carbon
H = % Hydrogen
O = % Oxygen
S = % Sulphur

content.title: Formula
content.code:
LCV = HCV - (0.09 × H × 587)

H = Percentage of hydrogen in the fuel

content.title: Calculation of Calorific Value
steps: Find % of C, H, O & S

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Dulong's Formula, the difference between HCV and LCV, and numerical problems based on these formulas are among the most frequently asked questions.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Calorific value is the heat released by complete combustion of fuel.
HCV includes latent heat of steam formed.
LCV excludes latent heat and is always less than HCV.
Dulong's Formula estimates HCV from elemental composition.
LCV can be calculated from HCV using the hydrogen correction.
